title: MATH GAOKAO - 144
description: Authentic-style mathematics problems inspired by China’s Gaokao — build deeper understanding, sharper thinking, and real exam readiness.

questions.learningObjective: Use the half-angle formula to find the cosine of half of an angle given the cosine of the angle and its quadrant.
questions.question: Given \(\cos\theta=\frac12\) and \(\theta\) lies in quadrant I, find \(\cos\frac{\theta}{2}\). Assume \(0<\theta<2\pi\).
questions.explanation:
Using the half-angle formula,
\[
\cos\frac{\theta}{2}=\sqrt{\frac{1+\cos\theta}{2}}.
\]
Substitute \(\cos\theta=\frac12\):
\[
\cos\frac{\theta}{2}=\sqrt{\frac{1+\frac12}{2}}=\sqrt{\frac{3/2}{2}}=\sqrt{\frac34}=\frac{\sqrt3}{2}.
\]
Since \(\theta\) is in quadrant I, \(\frac{\theta}{2}\) is also in quadrant I, so the cosine is positive.
questions.hint: Use the half-angle formula for cosine and determine the sign from the quadrant.

questions.learningObjective: Use the half-angle formula to find the sine of half of an angle given the sine of the angle and its quadrant.
questions.question: Given \(\sin\theta=\frac45\) and \(\theta\) lies in quadrant I, find \(\sin\frac{\theta}{2}\). Assume \(0<\theta<2\pi\).
questions.explanation:
Since \(\theta\) is in quadrant I and \(\sin\theta=\frac45\),
\[
\cos\theta=\sqrt{1-\left(\frac45\right)^2}=\sqrt{\frac{9}{25}}=\frac35.
\]
Using the half-angle formula,
\[
\sin\frac{\theta}{2}=\sqrt{\frac{1-\cos\theta}{2}}.
\]
Substitute \(\cos\theta=\frac35\):
\[
\sin\frac{\theta}{2}=\sqrt{\frac{1-\frac35}{2}}=\sqrt{\frac{2/5}{2}}=\sqrt{\frac15}=\frac{\sqrt5}{5}.
\]
Since \(\theta\) is in quadrant I, \(\frac{\theta}{2}\) is also in quadrant I, so the sine is positive.
questions.hint: First find \(\cos\theta\) using the Pythagorean identity, then apply the half-angle formula for sine.

questions.learningObjective: Use the half-angle formula to find the tangent of half of an angle given the tangent of the angle and its quadrant.
questions.question: Given \(\tan\theta=\frac34\) and \(\theta\) lies in quadrant III, find \(\tan\frac{\theta}{2}\).
questions.explanation:
Since \(\theta\) is in quadrant III, both \(\sin\theta\) and \(\cos\theta\) are negative. From \(\tan\theta=\frac34\), take the reference triangle with opposite side \(3\) and adjacent side \(4\). The hypotenuse is
\[
\sqrt{3^2+4^2}=5.
\]
Thus
\[
\sin\theta=-\frac35,\qquad \cos\theta=-\frac45.
\]
Using the half-angle formula,
\[
\tan\frac{\theta}{2}=\frac{\sin\theta}{1+\cos\theta}.
\]
Substitute the values:
\[
\tan\frac{\theta}{2}=\frac{-\frac35}{1-\frac45}=\frac{-\frac35}{\frac15}=-3.
\]
Therefore, \(\tan\frac{\theta}{2}=-3\).
questions.hint: Use \(\tan\frac{\theta}{2}=\frac{\sin\theta}{1+\cos\theta}\), and determine the signs from quadrant III.

questions.question: Evaluate \(\sin 15^\circ\).
questions.explanation:
Write \(15^\circ=\frac{30^\circ}{2}\). Using the half-angle formula for sine,
\[
\sin 15^\circ=\sqrt{\frac{1-\cos 30^\circ}{2}}.
\]
Since \(\cos 30^\circ=\frac{\sqrt3}{2}\),
\[
\sin 15^\circ=\sqrt{\frac{1-\frac{\sqrt3}{2}}{2}}=\sqrt{\frac{2-\sqrt3}{4}}=\frac{\sqrt{2-\sqrt3}}{2}.
\]
This can be rewritten as
\[
\frac{\sqrt6-\sqrt2}{4}.
\]
Therefore, \(\sin 15^\circ=\frac{\sqrt6-\sqrt2}{4}\).
questions.hint: Use the half-angle formula for sine with \(30^\circ\) and simplify.

questions.question: Evaluate \(\cos 22.5^\circ\).
questions.explanation:
Write \(22.5^\circ=\frac{45^\circ}{2}\). Using the half-angle formula for cosine,
\[
\cos 22.5^\circ=\sqrt{\frac{1+\cos 45^\circ}{2}}.
\]
Since \(\cos 45^\circ=\frac{\sqrt2}{2}\),
\[
\cos 22.5^\circ=\sqrt{\frac{1+\frac{\sqrt2}{2}}{2}}=\sqrt{\frac{2+\sqrt2}{4}}=\frac{\sqrt{2+\sqrt2}}{2}.
\]
Therefore, \(\cos 22.5^\circ=\frac{\sqrt{2+\sqrt2}}{2}\).
questions.hint: Use the half-angle formula for cosine with \(45^\circ\) and simplify.

questions.learningObjective: Use the half-angle formula to find the cosine of half of an angle given the cosine of the angle and its quadrant.
questions.question: Given \(\cos\theta=-\frac35\) and \(\theta\) lies in quadrant II, find \(\cos\frac{\theta}{2}\). Assume \(0<\theta<2\pi\).
questions.explanation:
Using the half-angle formula,
\[
\cos\frac{\theta}{2}=\sqrt{\frac{1+\cos\theta}{2}}.
\]
Substitute \(\cos\theta=-\frac35\):
\[
\cos\frac{\theta}{2}=\sqrt{\frac{1-\frac35}{2}}=\sqrt{\frac{2/5}{2}}=\sqrt{\frac15}=\frac{\sqrt5}{5}.
\]
Since \(\theta\) is in quadrant II, \(\frac{\theta}{2}\) lies in quadrant I, so the cosine is positive. Therefore, \(\cos\frac{\theta}{2}=\frac{\sqrt5}{5}\).
questions.hint: Use the half-angle formula for cosine and determine the sign from the quadrant of \(\frac{\theta}{2}\).

questions.learningObjective: Use the half-angle formula to find the tangent of half of an angle given the sine and cosine of the angle.
questions.question: Given \(\sin\theta=\frac35\) and \(\cos\theta=\frac45\), find \(\tan\frac{\theta}{2}\).
questions.explanation:
Using the half-angle formula for tangent,
\[
\tan\frac{\theta}{2}=\frac{\sin\theta}{1+\cos\theta}.
\]
Substitute \(\sin\theta=\frac35\) and \(\cos\theta=\frac45\):
\[
\tan\frac{\theta}{2}=\frac{\frac35}{1+\frac45}=\frac{\frac35}{\frac95}=\frac13.
\]
Therefore, \(\tan\frac{\theta}{2}=\frac13\).

questions.question: Evaluate \(\tan 15^\circ\).
questions.explanation:
Write \(15^\circ=\frac{30^\circ}{2}\). Using the half-angle formula for tangent,
\[
\tan 15^\circ=\frac{1-\cos 30^\circ}{\sin 30^\circ}.
\]
Since \(\cos 30^\circ=\frac{\sqrt3}{2}\) and \(\sin 30^\circ=\frac12\),
\[
\tan 15^\circ=\frac{1-\frac{\sqrt3}{2}}{\frac12}=2-\sqrt3.
\]
Therefore, \(\tan 15^\circ=2-\sqrt3\).
questions.hint: Use the half-angle formula for tangent with \(30^\circ\) and simplify.

questions.learningObjective: Use the half-angle formula to find the sine of half of an angle given the tangent of the angle and its quadrant.
questions.question: Given \(\tan\theta=\frac43\) and \(\theta\) lies in quadrant III, find \(\sin\frac{\theta}{2}\). Assume \(0<\theta<2\pi\).
questions.explanation:
Since \(\theta\) is in quadrant III, both \(\sin\theta\) and \(\cos\theta\) are negative. From \(\tan\theta=\frac43\), take the reference triangle with opposite side \(4\) and adjacent side \(3\). The hypotenuse is
\[
\sqrt{4^2+3^2}=5.
\]
Thus
\[
\sin\theta=-\frac45,\qquad \cos\theta=-\frac35.
\]
Using the half-angle formula for sine,
\[
\sin\frac{\theta}{2}=\sqrt{\frac{1-\cos\theta}{2}}.
\]
Substitute \(\cos\theta=-\frac35\):
\[
\sin\frac{\theta}{2}=\sqrt{\frac{1+\frac35}{2}}=\sqrt{\frac{8/5}{2}}=\sqrt{\frac45}=\frac{2\sqrt5}{5}.
\]
Since \(\theta\) is in quadrant III, \(\frac{\theta}{2}\) lies in quadrant II, where sine is positive. Therefore, \(\sin\frac{\theta}{2}=\frac{2\sqrt5}{5}\).
questions.hint: First determine \(\sin\theta\) and \(\cos\theta\) from the given tangent and quadrant, then use the half-angle formula for sine.

questions.learningObjective: Use the half-angle formula to find the cosine of half of an angle given the sine of the angle and its quadrant.
questions.question: Given \(\sin\theta=\frac13\) and \(\theta\) lies in quadrant II, find \(\cos\frac{\theta}{2}\). Assume \(0<\theta<2\pi\).
questions.explanation:
Since \(\theta\) is in quadrant II and \(\sin\theta=\frac13\),
\[
\cos\theta=-\sqrt{1-\left(\frac13\right)^2}=-\sqrt{\frac89}=-\frac{2\sqrt2}{3}.
\]
Using the half-angle formula for cosine,
\[
\cos\frac{\theta}{2}=\sqrt{\frac{1+\cos\theta}{2}}.
\]
Substitute \(\cos\theta=-\frac{2\sqrt2}{3}\):
\[
\cos\frac{\theta}{2}=\sqrt{\frac{1-\frac{2\sqrt2}{3}}{2}}=\sqrt{\frac{3-2\sqrt2}{6}}.
\]
Since \(3-2\sqrt2=(\sqrt2-1)^2\),
\[
\cos\frac{\theta}{2}=\frac{\sqrt2-1}{\sqrt6}.
\]
Since \(\theta\) is in quadrant II, \(\frac{\theta}{2}\) lies in quadrant I, so the cosine is positive. Therefore, \(\cos\frac{\theta}{2}=\frac{\sqrt2-1}{\sqrt6}\).
questions.hint: Find \(\cos\theta\) from the Pythagorean identity and quadrant, then use the half-angle formula for cosine. Simplify the radical using \(3-2\sqrt2=(\sqrt2-1)^2\).
